title: A Skid Steer Controller That Knows Slip: The Track It Really Turns On, the Speed the Ground Allows in a Turn, and Why the Plain Follower Slides Wide

questions.question: Why does a skid steer vehicle turn less than the plain track geometry says?
options: Its motors are weaker in a turn
The wheels slide sideways: the effective track is chi times the real one
Its wheels are too far apart
The ground pushes back harder on the inside
questions.explanation: All four wheels point straight ahead, so turning drags them sideways. The body turns as if the track were chi times wider, 1.5 times on tarmac here.

questions.question: Holding the path on tarmac: aware against unaware, the worst error was:
options: 0.042 m against 0.115 m
0.115 m against 0.042 m
0.042 m for both
0.000 m against 0.115 m
questions.explanation: A controller that takes chi as 1 asks for too small a difference in wheel speeds and slides wide of every bend. Knowing chi and the slip held the path to 0.042 m.

questions.question: On ice at 1.2 m/s the plain controller let go in how many steps?
options: 0, as with the limited controller
All of them
questions.explanation: At 1.2 m/s the bend asked for more sideways grip than ice has. The controller that capped its speed in the bend let go in 0 steps.

questions.question: How many times the speed does the same curve allow on gravel than on ice?
options: The same speed
Twice the ratio of the frictions
Half the speed
questions.explanation: The speed at which a curve lets go goes as the root of the friction. The ratio of the two speeds was 2.12.

questions.question: What does the limited controller give up?
options: Time: 5.4 s against 4.6 s on ice
Accuracy: it strays further from the path
The slip compensation
Nothing: it was faster as well
questions.explanation: The plain controller finished sooner by sliding. The limited one took 0.8 s more and stayed on the path.

questions.question: Why is there a floor on the speed in a turn?
options: To keep the motors cool
So the slip estimate stays valid
A controller that can command zero in a turn never gets out of it
Because pure pursuit needs a minimum speed
questions.explanation: If the cap can reach zero, a sharp enough curve stops the vehicle, and a stopped vehicle never leaves the curve.
